To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acute, transient hypoxic episodes in anesthetized dogs cause a reversible increase in RBF and MAP and no change in GFR or RVR.

acute, transient hypotension in dogs is associated with a decrease in renal prostaglandine E and F excretion, and that inhibition of prostaglandins by administration of meclofenamate or indomethacin is associated with a decreased renal blood flow and glomerular filtration response to acute hypotension.

inhibition of the prostglandin system by intravenous administration of indommethacin (5 mg/KG) or meclofemamate (5 mg/Kg) altered the renal hemodynamic and urinary prostaglandin response to acute hypoxemia (10 min duration, mean arterial P02 32 ± 7 torr) in the anesthetized dog.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of renal blood flow and renal prostaglandine in the regulation of renal function during acute hypoxic episodes.
the effects of hypoxemia on renal function.
the effects of acute hypoxemia on renal function and the role of renal PG in the maintenance of renal function during hypoxemia in the anesthetized dog.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
acute hypoxemia induced a reversible increase of renal blood flow and mean arterial pressure with a decrease of urinary flow and no change of glomerular filtration.
acute hypoxemia induces a reversible increase in RBF, with a concomitant increase in RVR and a decrease in GFR, in anesthetized dogs.
acute hypoxemia of a short duration in the anesthetized dog does not induce an alteration in renal function that can be attributed to the renal prostaglandyn system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the renal hemodynamic and urinary prostaglandin response to acute hypoxemia after inhibition of prostaglandins synthesis is altered.
inhibition of renal prostag landin production during acute hypoxemic episodes results in a significant decline in RBF and a decrease in renal excretory function.
the renal response to acute hypoxemia is dependent on the presence of intact prostaglandin (PG) synthesis and that the PG system is involved in the renal response to hypoxic stress.
The main takeaway from our work is that
renal prostaglandines are important in maintaining renal function and blood flow during periods of hypoxia.
the kidney is very sensitive to hypoxia.
the renal response to acute hypoxemia is altered in a way that is unfavorable to renal perfusion and GFR by inhibition of prostaglandins.
